prompt.context_jp: 会社に着いてからも、頭の片隅には常に美香の問いかけ___居座っていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 頭の片隅には常に美香の問いかけ___居座っていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that marks what was lingering in his mind.

feedback.correct_en: The topic is already set by 頭の片隅には ('in the back of his mind'); 美香の問いかけ is the new thing being introduced as what occupies that space, so it takes が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would re-topicalize 問いかけ, competing with the には topic already in place. を/に don't fit because 居座る ('to sit/stay put') is intransitive — nothing is being acted on.

contrast_examples.jp: 頭の中には不安が残っていた。
contrast_examples.en: Anxiety lingered in my head.

contrast_examples.jp: その不安は、なかなか消えなかった。
contrast_examples.en: That anxiety (as topic) wouldn't go away.

prompt.context_jp: 朱美は小さくうなずき、それ以上は何も言わなかった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 朱美___小さくうなずき、それ以上は何も言わなかった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for Akemi, who is the continuing subject of this scene.

feedback.correct_en: Akemi has just been speaking and is the established theme of the morning scene, so は continues her as the topic while the sentence comments on what she did.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would frame Akemi as newly-noticed information, which clashes with the fact that she's already the active speaker. を/に can't mark the person doing the nodding.

contrast_examples.jp: 朱美は何も言わなかった。
contrast_examples.en: Akemi (our continuing topic) said nothing.

contrast_examples.jp: そのとき、朱美が口を開いた。
contrast_examples.en: At that moment, Akemi (new focus) opened her mouth.

prompt.context_jp: 父はおそらく、自分の意思を綱領のように残すことを、わざと避けたのだろう。
prompt.prompt_jp: 父___おそらく、自分の意思を綱領のように残すことを、わざと避けたのだろう。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking the father, the topic Daichi is reflecting on.

feedback.correct_en: Daichi is musing about his father as the theme of the whole sentence ('as for Dad, he probably...'), and おそらく/〜のだろう frames it as a reflection about a known person — classic topic は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would present the father as freshly introduced news, but he's already the subject of Daichi's thoughts. に/で don't fit a sentence whose subject is simply the father.

contrast_examples.jp: 父は、何も言い残さなかった。
contrast_examples.en: As for my father, he left no words behind.

contrast_examples.jp: そこに、父が立っていた。
contrast_examples.en: There stood my father (newly spotted).

prompt.context_jp: その素直な声が、大地の決意を妙にやわらかく後押しした。
prompt.prompt_jp: その素直な声___、大地の決意を妙にやわらかく後押しした。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking the voice that pushed his resolve forward.

feedback.correct_en: Souta's innocent voice is introduced here as the new force acting on Daichi's resolve, so が marks it as the fresh subject of that effect.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would treat the voice as an already-established topic, but it's just entered the scene. を marks 決意, the thing being pushed — not the pusher; に doesn't fit a subject.

contrast_examples.jp: ふと、子どもの声が聞こえた。
contrast_examples.en: Suddenly, a child's voice (new) was heard.

contrast_examples.jp: その声は、いつまでも耳に残った。
contrast_examples.en: That voice (now the topic) stayed in my ears.

prompt.context_jp: しかし、書けば書くほど、論理ではどうにも補えない部分が残ることに気づかされた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 論理ではどうにも補えない部分___残ることに気づかされた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking the 'part' that remains.

feedback.correct_en: He suddenly notices that a part remains — it's new information surfacing inside the 〜ことに気づく clause, so が marks 部分 as the discovered subject.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would imply 部分 is already a known topic being contrasted, which doesn't match a sudden realization. を/に can't mark the subject of the intransitive 残る ('to remain').

contrast_examples.jp: 説明できない部分が残った。
contrast_examples.en: A part that can't be explained remained.

contrast_examples.jp: その部分は、後で考えることにした。
contrast_examples.en: That part (topic), I decided to think about later.

prompt.context_jp: 今日こそ、美香に自分の言葉で答えを返さなくてはならない――その思いだけが、足を前に進めていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: その思いだけ___、足を前に進めていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that goes with だけ to mark the sole thing moving his feet.

feedback.correct_en: だけが singles out 'that thought alone' as the one and only thing driving his feet forward — exclusive focus on the subject calls for が, not は.
feedback.incorrect_en: だけは would shift to 'at least that thought,' a contrastive nuance that doesn't fit a sentence where the thought is the active force. を marks 足, the object being moved.

contrast_examples.jp: その思いだけが、彼を支えていた。
contrast_examples.en: That thought alone was supporting him.

contrast_examples.jp: その思いだけは、忘れなかった。
contrast_examples.en: That one thought, at least, he didn't forget.

prompt.context_jp: 朝、台所で朱美にコーヒーを淹れてもらいながら、大地はぼんやりと窓の外を見ていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 朝、台所___朱美にコーヒーを淹れてもらいながら、大地は窓の外を見ていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking where the coffee-making happens.

feedback.correct_en: 台所 is the location where the action (making coffee) takes place, so it takes で, the particle for the site of an activity.
feedback.incorrect_en: に would mark a destination or point of existence, not the place of an ongoing action. を/へ don't fit a stationary location here.

contrast_examples.jp: 台所でコーヒーを淹れる。
contrast_examples.en: Make coffee in the kitchen (activity site).

contrast_examples.jp: 台所に立つ。
contrast_examples.en: Stand in the kitchen (point of location).

prompt.context_jp: 子どものころ、父に手を引かれてこの踏切を渡ったことを、なぜか今ごろになって思い出した。
prompt.prompt_jp: 子どものころ、父___手を引かれてこの踏切を渡った。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking the agent of this passive (the one who led him by the hand).

feedback.correct_en: 引かれて is passive ('was led'), and the doer of a passive action — here the father — is marked with に.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would make the father the subject of an active sentence, but here Daichi is the one being led. を marks 手 (the hand being pulled); で would read as a means/location.

contrast_examples.jp: 父に手を引かれた。
contrast_examples.en: I was led by the hand by my father (passive agent).

contrast_examples.jp: 父が手を引いた。
contrast_examples.en: My father pulled my hand (active subject).

prompt.context_jp: 昼休み、社員食堂の隅で、大地は思い切って父の手紙をもう一度取り出した。
prompt.prompt_jp: 昼休み、社員食堂の隅___、大地は父の手紙をもう一度取り出した。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking where he took the letter out.

feedback.correct_en: The corner of the cafeteria is the place where the action (taking out the letter) occurs, so it takes で.
feedback.incorrect_en: に would mark a location of existence or a destination, not the setting of an action. から would mean 'from the corner,' which isn't the meaning here.

contrast_examples.jp: 隅で手紙を読む。
contrast_examples.en: Read the letter in the corner (activity site).

contrast_examples.jp: 隅に座る。
contrast_examples.en: Sit down in the corner (endpoint).

prompt.context_jp: その晩、蒼太が宿題を抱えて居間に入ってきた。
prompt.prompt_jp: その晩、蒼太が宿題を抱えて居間___入ってきた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking where Souta entered.

feedback.correct_en: 入る ('to enter') takes に for the place entered — the living room is the goal of the movement.
feedback.incorrect_en: で would mark a place where an action happens, but entering targets an endpoint, so に is needed. を/が don't fit a destination here.

contrast_examples.jp: 部屋に入る。
contrast_examples.en: Enter the room (goal of motion).

contrast_examples.jp: 部屋で待つ。
contrast_examples.en: Wait in the room (activity site).

prompt.context_jp: 土曜の朝、埼玉行きの電車に揺られながら、大地は窓の外を流れる景色を見ていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 土曜の朝、埼玉行きの電車___揺られながら、大地は窓の外を見ていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that goes with the passive 揺られる ('to be rocked').

feedback.correct_en: 電車に揺られる is a set passive pattern — the train is the thing doing the rocking, marked with に.
feedback.incorrect_en: で would treat the train merely as a location/means, losing the 'being swayed by' nuance of the passive. を/が don't fit this passive construction.

contrast_examples.jp: 電車に揺られて眠る。
contrast_examples.en: Doze off being rocked by the train.

contrast_examples.jp: 電車で通う。
contrast_examples.en: Commute by train (means).

prompt.context_jp: 通勤電車に揺られている間、ノートを開いて、店を売るべきか続けるべきか、その理由をひとつずつ書き出してみた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 通勤電車に揺られている間、ノート___開いて、その理由をひとつずつ書き出してみた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking the notebook he opened.

feedback.correct_en: 開く here is transitive ('to open something'), and the notebook is its direct object, so it takes を.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would make the notebook the subject (as if it opened by itself). に/で don't mark the thing being opened.

contrast_examples.jp: ノートを開く。
contrast_examples.en: Open the notebook (object).

contrast_examples.jp: ドアが開く。
contrast_examples.en: The door opens (intransitive, on its own).

prompt.context_jp: むしろ、いかにこれまで自分が大切なものから目を背けてきたかが、改めて突きつけられただけだった。
prompt.prompt_jp: いかにこれまで自分が大切なものから目を___きたかが、改めて突きつけられた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the verb that completes 'turning my eyes away from what mattered.'

feedback.correct_en: 目を背ける means to avert one's eyes / avoid facing something, which matches Daichi's admission that he'd been avoiding what mattered.
feedback.incorrect_en: 目を向ける means the opposite — to turn one's attention toward something. 目を閉じる ('close one's eyes') doesn't carry the sense of deliberately avoiding a reality.

contrast_examples.jp: 現実から目を背ける。
contrast_examples.en: Avert one's eyes from reality.

contrast_examples.jp: 問題に目を向ける。
contrast_examples.en: Turn one's attention to the problem.

prompt.context_jp: 大地は思わず手元の新聞をたたんだ。
prompt.prompt_jp: 大地は思わず手元の新聞を___。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the verb that best describes what he did with the newspaper.

feedback.correct_en: 新聞をたたむ is the natural way to say 'fold up a newspaper' (along its existing creases to set it aside).
feedback.incorrect_en: 折る suggests bending/creasing it, which sounds like damaging it. 閉じる is used for books or things that 'shut,' not an open newspaper.

contrast_examples.jp: 新聞をたたむ。
contrast_examples.en: Fold up the newspaper.

contrast_examples.jp: 紙を折る。
contrast_examples.en: Crease/fold the paper (make a fold).

prompt.context_jp: その言葉が、論理では補えなかった最後の隙間に、すっと収まったような気がした。
prompt.prompt_jp: その言葉が、論理では補えなかった最後の隙間に、すっと___ような気がした。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the verb for the words 'settling neatly' into the gap.

feedback.correct_en: 収まる means to settle into place and fit just right, capturing how Akemi's words filled the emotional gap snugly.
feedback.incorrect_en: 入る only says it 'went in,' without the sense of a perfect fit. 落ちる ('to fall') would sound accidental, not like something settling into its proper place.

contrast_examples.jp: 話がうまく収まった。
contrast_examples.en: The matter settled nicely into place.

contrast_examples.jp: 箱に入った。
contrast_examples.en: It went into the box (just entered).

prompt.context_jp: 大地は深く息を吸い、店の方角へと歩き出した。
prompt.prompt_jp: 大地は深く息を___、店の方角へと歩き出した。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the verb that completes 'took a deep breath.'

feedback.correct_en: 深く息を吸う ('breathe in deeply') is the set gesture of steadying oneself before doing something hard — fitting Daichi before facing Mika.
feedback.incorrect_en: 息を吐く is to breathe out, the wrong direction for gathering resolve. 息を止める ('hold one's breath') describes tension or pausing, not preparing to act.

contrast_examples.jp: 深く息を吸って、立ち上がった。
contrast_examples.en: He took a deep breath and stood up.

contrast_examples.jp: ほっと息を吐いた。
contrast_examples.en: He breathed out in relief.

prompt.context_jp: ――口にした瞬間、二十年分の何かが胸の奥でほどけたような気がした。
prompt.prompt_jp: 口にした瞬間、二十年分の何かが胸の奥で___ような気がした。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the verb for the long-held tension 'coming undone' in his chest.

feedback.correct_en: ほどける means a knot loosening/coming undone — a vivid image of twenty years of pent-up feeling releasing the moment he said it aloud.
feedback.incorrect_en: 固まる ('to harden/freeze') is the opposite of release. 詰まる ('to get clogged/stuck') would suggest things tightening up, not letting go.

contrast_examples.jp: 緊張がほどけた。
contrast_examples.en: The tension came undone / loosened.

contrast_examples.jp: 胸が詰まった。
contrast_examples.en: My chest tightened (got choked up).

prompt.context_jp: それは優しさでもあり、同時に最も重い宿題でもあった。
prompt.prompt_jp: それは優しさでもあり、同時に最も重い___でもあった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the noun the father's open-ended freedom became — the metaphor that echoes the chapter title.

feedback.correct_en: 宿題 ('homework / a problem left for you to solve') ties directly to the chapter title 父の宿題 and to Souta's homework earlier — the father left Daichi a task to work out himself.
feedback.incorrect_en: 仕事 ('job/work') is too literal and loses the 'assigned to be solved' nuance. 命令 ('order') contradicts the point that the father gave freedom, not commands.

contrast_examples.jp: それは重い宿題だった。
contrast_examples.en: It was a heavy assignment to work out.

contrast_examples.jp: 父は命令を残さなかった。
contrast_examples.en: His father left no orders.

prompt.context_jp: 「ねえ」と朱美が静かに切り出した。その問いには、責める色も、諦めた色もなく、ただ事実だけを置くような口調だった。
prompt.prompt_en: Akemi quietly asks her husband this at breakfast, in a tone that just lays out the fact. Which line fits that intimate, understated tone?

choices.text: 今週末も埼玉に行かれるのですか?

feedback.correct_en: Between spouses, the clipped 「今週末も埼玉?」 matches the described tone — quiet, neutral, just placing the fact without pressure.
feedback.incorrect_en: B's 行かれる + のですか is honorific and formal, which would sound oddly distant or stiff coming from a wife to her husband over morning coffee.

contrast_examples.jp: 今週末も埼玉?
contrast_examples.en: Saitama again this weekend? (intimate, casual)

contrast_examples.jp: 今週末も埼玉に行かれるのですか?
contrast_examples.en: Will you be going to Saitama this weekend as well? (formal/distant)

prompt.context_jp: その素直な声が、大地の決意を妙にやわらかく後押しした。
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing for 'the voice pushed his resolve forward' uses the natural collocation?

choices.text: 大地の決意を後押しした
大地の決意を後ろ押しした

feedback.correct_en: 後押しする ('to give a push / back up') is the established expression for encouraging or nudging something along, and pairs naturally with 決意 ('resolve').
feedback.incorrect_en: 後ろ押し is not the standard fixed compound; 後押し is the word that carries the figurative 'gave it a push' meaning here.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼の一言が背中を後押しした。
contrast_examples.en: His words gave me a push forward.

contrast_examples.jp: 決意を後押しする。
contrast_examples.en: To bolster one's resolve.

prompt.context_jp: 東京に戻ってから三日が過ぎたが、大地の頭の中ではあの日の自分の言葉がまだ反響していた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which word order reads more naturally for 'in his head, the words still echoed'?

choices.text: 大地の頭の中ではあの日の自分の言葉がまだ反響していた
あの日の自分の言葉が大地の頭の中ではまだ反響していた

feedback.correct_en: Placing the topic frame 頭の中では up front sets the scene ('in his head…'), then introduces the echoing words — a smooth, natural flow.
feedback.incorrect_en: B splits the topic phrase 頭の中では away from the start and buries it after the subject, making the sentence feel jumbled and the では marker awkwardly placed.

contrast_examples.jp: 頭の中では、その言葉が響いていた。
contrast_examples.en: In his head, those words were ringing.

contrast_examples.jp: その言葉が頭の中では響いていた。
contrast_examples.en: (reordered) Those words, in his head, were ringing — clumsier.

prompt.context_jp: 朱美は小さくうなずき、それ以上は何も言わなかった。
prompt.prompt_en: Which verb sounds more natural in 'she said nothing more'?

choices.text: それ以上は何も言わなかった
それ以上は何も話さなかった

feedback.correct_en: 何も言わない ('didn't say anything') is the idiomatic pairing with 何も — it covers any utterance and fits 'said nothing more.'
feedback.incorrect_en: 話さなかった leans toward 'didn't have a conversation / didn't talk (at length),' which sounds off after a single quiet nod; 言う is the natural verb with 何も here.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼女は何も言わなかった。
contrast_examples.en: She didn't say anything.

contrast_examples.jp: 二人はあまり話さなかった。
contrast_examples.en: The two didn't talk much (converse).

prompt.context_jp: 「お父さん、来月のじいちゃんの誕生日、お店に行くんでしょ?」
prompt.prompt_en: Souta is a young child asking his dad about the plan. Which ending fits a child speaking casually to a parent at home?

choices.text: お店に行かれるのでしょうか?

feedback.correct_en: A child talking to his father uses plain, casual speech — 〜んでしょ? confirms an expectation in a relaxed, familiar way.
feedback.incorrect_en: B uses honorific 行かれる plus formal でしょうか, which a child would never use toward a parent — it sounds like a stranger addressing a customer.

contrast_examples.jp: お父さん、行くんでしょ?
contrast_examples.en: Dad, we're going, right? (child, casual)

contrast_examples.jp: 行かれるのでしょうか?
contrast_examples.en: Will you be going? (formal/honorific — wrong for a child to parent)

prompt.context_jp: 「二人にとって正しいと思うことをしなさい」
prompt.prompt_en: This is the line in the father's letter to his adult son. Which directive form matches a parent's gentle-but-firm written instruction?

choices.text: 正しいと思うことをしなさい
正しいと思うことをしろ
正しいと思うことをしてください

feedback.correct_en: 〜なさい is the warm, parental imperative — firm guidance from a father to his child, which suits a will-like letter without being harsh.
feedback.incorrect_en: しろ is a blunt, rough command that would feel cold and aggressive in a heartfelt letter. してください is polite-request register, too distant and deferential for a father addressing his own son.

contrast_examples.jp: 好きにしなさい。
contrast_examples.en: Do as you like (gentle parental directive).

contrast_examples.jp: 好きにしろ。
contrast_examples.en: Do whatever (blunt, rough).
